title: bug: PowerShell 5.1 reads UTF-8 .moe-agent.json non-ASCII serenaProject using ANSI encoding
description: Get-Content -Raw -Path $moeAgentConfig (and with -LiteralPath) omits -Encoding UTF8. A BOM-less UTF-8 JSON serenaProject pointing at an existing directory containing é becomes mojibake on PS5.1 and falls back to project root with override not found; pwsh7 reads it correctly. Independently reproduced during task-3ad573a7; its fixture can use a BOM to isolate wildcard behavior.
definitionOfDone: PS5.1 honors BOM-less UTF-8 serenaProject with non-ASCII directory names.
Regression covers PS5.1 and pwsh7 reads without changing missing-path fallback behavior.
Keep literal-path binding from task-3ad573a7 if present.

implementationPlan.description:
RED, then fix. Work from the task checkout root: `cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"`. This row dependsOn task-3ad573a7, so at claim time its literal-path edits have landed:
- the line reads `$cfg = Get-Content -Raw -LiteralPath $moeAgentConfig | ConvertFrom-Json`;
- scripts/tests/literal-project-path.test.mjs exists.
Check both with grep first. Write tracked files only with the Edit/Write tools.

(1) New scripts/tests/serena-project-config.test.mjs (node:test, ESM). Header comment: PS 5.1's Get-Content reads a BOM-less file as ANSI, so a UTF-8 .moe-agent.json whose serenaProject names a non-ASCII directory became mojibake and fell back to the project root. JSON is UTF-8 (RFC 8259).

Read `new URL('../moe-agent.ps1', import.meta.url)`, strip the BOM and convert CRLF to LF. Cut `block = between(ps, '\n$serenaProject = $projectPath.ToString()', '\nif ($serenaPath -and ')` with a `between` that asserts both anchors exist, like daemon-json-cap.test.mjs:23-28.

Tests:

(a) Static, every OS: the block's Get-Content line that reads `$moeAgentConfig` contains `-Encoding UTF8` and `-LiteralPath $moeAgentConfig`. Drop the -LiteralPath assertion only if 3ad573a7 was archived without landing, and say so in the summary. This is RED on today's line.

(b) Engines: copy daemon-json-cap.test.mjs's `probe()` and its two ps1 rows (:53-60):
- PowerShell 5.1 = powershell.exe, Windows-only, skip elsewhere with that reason;
- PowerShell 7 = pwsh.exe on win32, else pwsh, skipped when the probe fails.

For each engine, three rows, each in its own `fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'moe-serena-'))`, rmSync'd in t.after (maxRetries 5):
- BOM-less UTF-8 naming an existing dir `serena é ü`;
- the same file with a leading ﻿ (back-compat);
- BOM-less naming a missing `absent é`.

For each row:
- Write `<root>/proj/.moe-agent.json` = (bom ? '﻿' : '') + JSON.stringify({ serenaProject: dir }). writeFileSync with a string writes UTF-8 without a BOM.
- Write a `﻿`-prefixed script: `$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'`, `[Console]::OutputEncoding = [Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)`, `$projectPath = <psq(project)>`, then `block`, then `Write-Output "SERENA=$serenaProject"` and `Write-Output "SOURCE=$serenaProjectSource"`.
- Run `spawnSync(exe, ['-NoProfile','-NonInteractive','-ExecutionPolicy','Bypass','-File', script], { encoding:'utf8', timeout:60000, windowsHide:true, env })`, with env = process.env minus /^MOE_/i so MOE_SERENA_PROJECT never leaks in.
- Assert status 0 and strip `\r`. Then:
  - Existing rows: SOURCE === '.moe-agent.json', realpathSync.native(SERENA).toLowerCase() === the dir's, and no `[WARN]`.
  - Missing row: SOURCE === 'project root (override not found)', SERENA === project, and the output includes exactly `[WARN] Serena project '<dir>' (from .moe-agent.json) not found; using Moe project root`. This is today's fallback, unchanged apart from the path now decoding correctly.

(2) Wire it into CI. In .github/workflows/ci.yml, right after the `Test launcher daemon.json cap and seat re-registration` step, add a step: name `Test PowerShell .moe-agent.json read`; one comment line (PowerShell 5.1 reads a BOM-less file as ANSI unless told UTF-8; Linux runs pwsh 7); `if: runner.os != 'macOS'`; `run: node --test scripts/tests/serena-project-config.test.mjs`.

RED:
- On Linux, `node --test scripts/tests/serena-project-config.test.mjs`: test (a) fails.
- Natively, `"/mnt/c/Program Files/nodejs/node.exe" --test "$(wslpath -w "$PWD/scripts/tests/serena-project-config.test.mjs")"`: the two BOM-less PowerShell 5.1 rows fail, with mojibake (`Ã©`) in SERENA or the WARN. The BOM row and every pwsh row pass.

Quote both failures in the completion summary.

(3) Fix scripts/moe-agent.ps1, in the .moe-agent.json read inside the Serena block (about :665). Make it `$cfg = Get-Content -Raw -LiteralPath $moeAgentConfig -Encoding UTF8 | ConvertFrom-Json`. Keep 3ad573a7's -LiteralPath (DoD 3) and every other token.
- `-Encoding UTF8` decodes UTF-8 on PS 5.1 and 7, and consumes a BOM when present, so BOM'd files keep working.
- Error handling: unchanged. The try/catch "Could not parse" WARN, the MOE_SERENA_PROJECT step and the not-found fallback stay byte for byte.
- Keep the file's UTF-8 BOM and LF endings.
- Change no other Get-Content site. The sibling PS 5.1 default-encoding reads (Load-Registry, project.json, KNOWN_ISSUES.md, the codex/gemini/grok configs) are out of scope and reported separately.

Re-run both RED commands: all green.
implementationPlan.note: RED: Linux static test failed (line lacked -Encoding UTF8); Windows PS5.1 BOM-less rows failed with mojibake 'serena Ã© Ã¼' in the WARN. Fixed: added -Encoding UTF8 to the one Get-Content line (BOM + LF kept); CI step added.

implementationPlan.description:
Adversarial self-review of this diff only:
- `git diff -U0 -- scripts/moe-agent.ps1` adds only ` -Encoding UTF8` to that one line. No -LiteralPath, -Raw or ConvertFrom-Json change.
- The BOM and LF endings are kept.
- The new test cleans every temp root even on assertion failure.
- Its env strips MOE_*, so a seat's MOE_SERENA_PROJECT cannot mask a failure.
- The anchors fail loudly when moved, through between()'s assert.
- Back-compat: an ANSI-encoded non-ASCII .moe-agent.json now decodes as UTF-8, with U+FFFD for the bad bytes, and falls back with the WARN. Accept this: such a file is not valid JSON per RFC 8259, and pwsh 7 and the sh twin already read UTF-8.
- The ci.yml step uses the same `if:` guard as its neighbour.

Fix anything found and re-run step 2 before complete_task.
implementationPlan.note: Self-review clean. The ps1 diff is one line and adds only -Encoding UTF8. The BOM (efbbbf) and LF endings are kept. The test registers t.after rmSync right after mkdtempSync. planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Rejected: extend 3ad573a7's literal-project-path.test.mjs fixture (drop its BOM, add a missing-path launch). Each case is a full real-wrapper launch of minutes, and that fixture's BOM deliberately isolates the wildcard behaviour.

Chosen: a focused cut-and-run test of the Serena block. It takes seconds per row on PS 5.1 and pwsh 7, and its 3 rows map to DoD 1 and 2.

Rejected: an ANSI fallback on invalid UTF-8. JSON is UTF-8, so it is not worth the complexity.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- The Serena block is moe-agent.ps1 :659-686, between `$serenaProject = $projectPath.ToString()` and `if ($serenaPath -and (Test-Path ...))`.
- daemon-json-cap.test.mjs already has the PS engine probe/table (:49-60) and the cut-and-run pattern (powershellKeys :590-604: a BOM'd script with Console UTF-8 output).
- 3ad573a7's fixture writes `.moe-agent.json` with a BOM precisely because of this bug (literal-project-path.test.mjs:130-131).
- PS 5.1 Get-Content without -Encoding also reads :167, :308, :978, :1030, :1238, :1379, :1545, :2822, :3894, :3915 and :4598. Out of scope, reported to the governor.
planningNotes.risks:
- Write-Host output reaches captured stdout only with [Console]::OutputEncoding set to UTF-8; without it, PS 5.1 rows mis-decode é even when fixed.
- os.tmpdir() on Windows may be an 8.3 short path. Compare SERENA through realpathSync.native, as literal-project-path.test.mjs does.
- The PS 5.1 rows only run natively on Windows; a Linux-only run is not evidence for DoD 1.
